newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian market rates steady, liquidity improved.
newsitem.headline: Croatian market rates steady, liquidity improved.

text.p: Croatian interbank call money rates remained mostly steady amid improved liquidity on Tuesday, dealers said.

"We are breathing somewhat easier today, although this is a short-term relief as the finances for the teachers' salaries and those of the Croatian army injected from the budget will be paid immediately," dealer Jasenka Blagaic told Reuters.
Fresh loans totalled 44.7 million kuna, most of which were call money borrowings granted at 10.5 percent with a single loan brokered at 11 percent, the latter borrowing made by a savings bank.
Due to the market still being somewhat strained, lenders chose to grant mostly call money loans and short term borrowings.
One 10-day loan was struck at 11 percent and a smaller 30-day deal made at 13 percent.
Some four million kuna were still sought after 0900 GMT.
Monday's overnight trade totalled 46.7 million kuna sought by one bank to square its position. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
